desc: Prove that \(f(x,y)\) is the smallest edge weight at which \(x\) and \(y\) belong to the same Kruskal/DSU component.
Derive the matching invariant: at threshold \(w\), the maximum number of pairs with cost at most \(w\) is the sum over components of \(\min(\text{countA},\text{countB})\).
Establish that a DSU merge contributes \(\min(a_1+a_2,b_1+b_2)-\min(a_1,b_1)-\min(a_2,b_2)\) newly feasible pairs, charged at the merge weight.
Confirm that processing equal-weight edges sequentially is safe because all merges at that weight are charged identically and the increments telescope.
Implement fast Python input parsing, weighted edge sorting, DSU unions, 64-bit-safe answer accumulation, and final output.
Verify the implementation on both sample cases and check duplicate-occurrence handling.
